units.text: 3. Irremovable doubts as to a person's guilt are interpreted in favour of the accused.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 49

units.text: Article 50
units.label: Art. 50

units.text: 1. No one may be convicted twice for the same crime.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 50

units.text: 2. Evidence obtained in violation of federal law may not be used in the administration of justice.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 50

units.text: 3. Everyone convicted of a crime has the right to have the judgment reviewed by a higher court in the manner established by federal law and the right to request a pardon or mitigation of punishment.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 50

units.text: Article 51
units.label: Art. 51

units.text: 1. No one is obliged to testify against themselves, their spouse or close relatives, whose scope is defined by federal law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 51

units.text: 2. Federal law may establish other cases of exemption from the obligation to give testimony.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 51

units.text: Article 52
units.label: Art. 52

units.text: The rights of victims of crimes and abuses of power are protected by law. The State ensures victims' access to justice and compensation for damage caused.
units.label: Art. 52 · text

units.text: Article 53
units.label: Art. 53

units.text: Everyone has the right to compensation by the State for harm caused by unlawful actions (or inaction) of bodies of state authority or their officials.
units.label: Art. 53 · text

units.text: Article 54
units.label: Art. 54

units.text: 1. A law establishing or increasing liability has no retroactive effect.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 54

units.text: 2. No one may be held liable for an act that was not recognized as an offence at the time it was committed. If liability for an offence is abolished or mitigated after its commission, the new law applies.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 54

units.text: Article 55
units.label: Art. 55

units.text: 1. The enumeration of fundamental rights and freedoms in the Constitution of the Russian Federation must not be interpreted as denying or diminishing other universally recognized human and civil rights and freedoms.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 55

units.text: 2. Laws abolishing or diminishing human and civil rights and freedoms must not be enacted in the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 55

units.text: 3. Human and civil rights and freedoms may be restricted by federal law only to the extent necessary to protect the foundations of the constitutional order, morality, health and the rights and lawful interests of others, and to ensure national defence and state security.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 55

units.text: Article 56
units.label: Art. 56

units.text: 1. During a state of emergency, specific restrictions on rights and freedoms may be established in accordance with federal constitutional law to ensure citizens' safety and protect the constitutional order, specifying their scope and duration.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 56

units.text: 2. A state of emergency throughout the territory of the Russian Federation or in particular localities may be introduced in the circumstances and in the manner established by federal constitutional law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 56

units.text: 3. The rights and freedoms provided for in Articles 20, 21, 23 (part 1), 24, 28, 34 (part 1), 40 (part 1) and 46–54 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be restricted.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 56

units.text: Article 57
units.label: Art. 57

units.text: Everyone is obliged to pay legally established taxes and levies. Laws introducing new taxes or worsening the position of taxpayers have no retroactive effect.
units.label: Art. 57 · text

units.text: Article 58
units.label: Art. 58

units.text: Everyone is obliged to preserve nature and the environment and to treat natural resources with care.
units.label: Art. 58 · text

units.text: Article 59
units.label: Art. 59

units.text: 1. Defence of the Fatherland is the duty and obligation of a citizen of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 59

units.text: 2. A citizen of the Russian Federation performs military service in accordance with federal law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 59

units.text: 3. A citizen of the Russian Federation whose beliefs or religion conflict with military service, and in other cases established by federal law, has the right to substitute alternative civilian service for it.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 59

units.text: Article 60
units.label: Art. 60

units.text: A citizen of the Russian Federation may independently exercise their rights and duties in full from the age of 18.
units.label: Art. 60 · text

units.text: Article 61
units.label: Art. 61

units.text: 1. A citizen of the Russian Federation may not be expelled from the Russian Federation or extradited to another State.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 61

units.text: 2. The Russian Federation guarantees its citizens protection and patronage outside its borders.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 61

units.text: Article 62
units.label: Art. 62

units.text: 1. A citizen of the Russian Federation may hold citizenship of a foreign State (dual citizenship) in accordance with federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 62

units.text: 2. A citizen of the Russian Federation's possession of foreign citizenship does not diminish their rights and freedoms or release them from duties arising from Russian citizenship, unless otherwise provided by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 62

units.text: 3. Foreign citizens and stateless persons in the Russian Federation enjoy rights and bear duties on an equal footing with citizens of the Russian Federation, except in cases established by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 62

units.text: Article 63
units.label: Art. 63

units.text: 1. The Russian Federation grants political asylum to foreign citizens and stateless persons in accordance with universally recognized rules of international law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 63

units.text: 2. The Russian Federation does not permit extradition to other States of persons persecuted for political beliefs or for actions (or inaction) not recognized as crimes in the Russian Federation. Extradition of persons accused of crimes and transfer of convicted persons to serve sentences in other States are carried out on the basis of federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 63

units.text: Article 64
units.label: Art. 64

units.text: The provisions of this chapter constitute the foundations of the legal status of the individual in the Russian Federation and may be changed only in the manner established by this Constitution.
units.label: Art. 64 · text

units.text: CHAPTER 3. FEDERAL STRUCTURE
units.label: CHAPTER 3. FEDERAL STRUCTURE
